answer: Temporal TTL binds each agent action to a decaying window: an echo of prior attestations must still fall inside the vertex of the current saffron-timed epoch or the signature expires. Operation: peers only countersign if the referenced history stamp is fresher than the TTL; older echoes are discarded before consensus. Attacker cost: a Sybil farm must re-mint and re-attest every identity on every epoch close, paying full compute and latency for each fresh window instead of amortizing one long-lived key across many cycles.
